subject: URGENT: throughput cliff after qprofile v2.1 swap — rollback request & exec sync
messages:
From: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@swiftpay.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@swiftpay.com
Date: Fri, 29 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95 spike & errors after 'qprofile v2.1' change

Sofia —

We started seeing a big regression across our payment authorization endpoint approximately 02:30 UTC after your recent qprofile v2.1 rollout.

Symptoms:
- p95 latency jumped from ~180ms to ~520ms within 10 minutes
- end-to-end throughput dropped by ~40% under typical load
- user-facing error rate rose to ~3.4% (timeouts + decode failures)

This is affecting checkout for a substantial portion of our traffic. Can you confirm whether this rollout touched our dedicated pool and what immediate mitigations you can apply? We need an ETA — or please rollback.

Alex
Alex Dunn
Head of Platform Engineering, SwiftPay
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@swiftpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Oct 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike & errors after 'qprofile v2.1' change

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. We're investigating right now. Initial checks: the qprofile v2.1 rollout targeted the SwiftPay dedicated pool as part of a staged canary (10% → 100%) and completed at ~02:10 UTC.

Immediate steps we're taking:
- Pulling telemetry and traces for the affected nodes
- Enabling expanded debug logging for the decode path
- Standing up an internal incident bridge (joining now)

Can we schedule a short maintenance window for an emergency rollback if needed? Karthik, can you confirm the feasibility of rolling back to v2.0 without a full model swap?

—Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Oct 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike & errors after 'qprofile v2.1' change

Sofia / team — quick tech note from runtime side after looking at decode traces and kernel metrics:

What we see:
- v2.1 qprofile changes reduce avg memory use but picked an aggressive int8 kernel for the model's attention block. On the dedicated A100 stovepipe SwiftPay runs, that kernel has a path that currently serializes some decode ops resulting in multithread contention under >300 req/s.
- There are repeated small kernel timeouts showing as decode failures (explains the 3.4% errors).
- KV cache hit rate unchanged, so not a cache issue.

Mitigation options (ranked):
1) Immediate rollback of qprofile v2.1 → v2.0 for SwiftPay pool (fastest; config flip, no model recompile).
2) Enable model_variant fallback to the fp16 variant for hot routes (auto-fallback if int8 kernel fails) — requires config push and quick canary (10–15 min).
3) If rollback not approved, throttle max concurrency on affected nodes and enable forced sequential decode (buying hours, but increases p99).

I recommend option 1 + option 2 as a safety net. I can run the rollback now if we have go-ahead; impact window ~10 minutes to flip and drain. Will attach kernel traces to the internal bundle.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Oct 2027 12:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec note: request approval for emergency rollback + customer credit conversation

Marissa / leadership — coupling technical recommendation with customer impact: SwiftPay is high-usage enterprise (large daily volumes). Karthik recommends an immediate rollback to qprofile v2.0 for their dedicated pool and enabling fp16 fallback while we debug the int8 kernel path.

Business asks:
- Approve emergency rollback for SWP-4821 (we'll target 20:00 UTC tonight — low traffic for SwiftPay).
- Approve offering 10% usage credit for the day of incident (CS cover).
- Exec sync at 16:00 UTC to review root cause timeline and customer comms.

If we approve, ops can run rollback with <15 mins disruption and we will push a post-mortem to the SwiftPay contacts within 48 hours.

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor
VP, Customer Success Operations
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@swiftpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 31 Oct 2027 17:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Action plan: rollback scheduled + what to expect (SwiftPay)

Alex —

Appreciate your patience. Summary and immediate plan:

Findings: kernel mismatch for the int8 path in qprofile v2.1 caused decode stalls under high concurrency, producing the p95 and error symptoms you reported.

Planned actions (timeline):
- 20:00 UTC (31 Oct): Emergency rollback qprofile v2.1 → v2.0 for SwiftPay dedicated pool (config flip, short drain).
- 20:10 UTC: Validate p95, throughput and error rate on canary subset; if green, roll to remaining nodes (target complete by 20:30 UTC).
- Post-rollback: enable fp16 fallback on hot routes and keep v2.1 disabled for SwiftPay until we push a patched qprofile.

What we need from you: permission to perform the rollback in the 20:00 UTC window and a brief maintenance window (10–30 minutes). We will share live dashboards and the support bundle (attached).

We will also offer a 10% usage credit for 31 Oct as a gesture while we resolve root causes.

If you approve, reply to this thread with "APPROVE ROLLBACK" and we'll proceed.

—Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: ppc_latency_graphs.png, support_bundle_20271031.zip
From: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@swiftpay.com>

Cc: SwiftPay Platform Team <platform@swiftpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 31 Oct 2027 18:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Action plan: rollback scheduled + what to expect (SwiftPay)

APPROVE ROLLBACK — please proceed with the 20:00 UTC window. We'll monitor from our side and stand by on the incident bridge. Thank you for the quick triage and clear plan.

Alex
